identity_levels.family: Shared name used for related flows in more than one basin; split before measuring.
identity_levels.system: A named circulation system that can contain branches or segments.
identity_levels.current: One named current with a source-dependent upstream and downstream extent.
identity_levels.segment: Named part or continuation of a larger current system.
identity_levels.eddy_family: A named class of related eddies, such as Agulhas Rings; individual members need separate dated identities.
identity_levels.recurrent_eddy_region: A geographic name reused for eddies forming or persisting in a region; not one dated individual or trajectory.
identity_levels.individual_eddy: A particular named eddy, separate from its type, region, and trajectory ID.
identity_levels.dated_detection: A feature designated by one provider in one dated receipt; no historical-name equivalence, formation time, lifetime, or continuity across dates is established.

claims.scope: Approximate circumpolar path; source calls it the longest wind-driven current.

NASA/JPL's 2019 overview says the Antarctic Circumpolar Current spans about 13,000 miles (21,000 km). It does not specify a reference streamline or contour, so this alternate whole-current approximation is retained separately from the ranked 25,000 km research estimate.
claims.source_locator: NASA/JPL article, paragraph beginning The Antarctic Circumpolar Current flows in a loop (13,000 miles / 21,000 km)

claims.scope: Approximate California Current System extent from Baja California Sur to northern Vancouver Island; not a measured California Current core axis.

claims.scope: Tomczak and Godfrey report approximately 2,500 km for the Gulf Stream proper as an open-ocean free jet downstream of Cape Hatteras toward the Newfoundland Rise/Grand Banks near 50°W. This excludes the Florida Current and North Atlantic Current; it is a textbook path-scale description, not a measured reference streamline. NOAA's glossary uses the same strict segment definition, while NASA and NOAA Coast Pilot sometimes use Gulf Stream more broadly.
claims.source_locator: Chapter 14, The Atlantic Ocean, PDF page 11 (printed page 239), paragraph beginning Recirculation of Gulf Stream water (next 2,500 km Gulf Stream proper)
PDF page 3, Section 2.1 Underwater Glider Data and Methods, paragraph on 52 missions sampling a roughly 2,000 km Gulf Stream reach

claims.scope: Approximate Kuroshio journey from about 12°N to 35°N in the western North Pacific; not a measured whole-current axis, and the Kuroshio Extension is separate.
claims.source_locator: PDF page 3, Introduction opening paragraph (3,000 km journey from about 12°N to 35°N)

claims.scope: The research description spans roughly 27°S–40°S; the coastal path is longer than its north–south separation. Retroflection, leakage, and the eastward Agulhas Return Current are distinct from this boundary-current core. The derived floor is unranked. A 2021 review also describes a roughly 1,000 km coastal segment. That narrower usage conflicts with the broader 27°S–40°S derived floor, so the two numbers are displayed as source-specific scopes and neither is ranked as a common whole-current length.
claims.source_locator: Section The Agulhas Current, opening paragraph (27–40°S); 1,400 km floor is OSW meridional gate geometry

claims.scope: Coastal western boundary current along southeastern Africa; narrower than the 27°S–40°S span used for the existing broad lower bound. End gates and centerline are not specified.
claims.source_locator: Section 2.1.1 Background, opening paragraph (1,000 km western boundary current)

claims.scope: The hydrographic survey distinguishes the Agulhas Return Current from the Agulhas Current and traces its weakening eastward flow toward the Crozet Basin. This derived distance floor is not a measured streamline, whole-current length, or the length of the westward Agulhas Current.
claims.source_locator: PDF pages 20–22, Figure 14 and Section 6 Conclusions, Agulhas Return Current surveyed eastward from 18°E to 76°E; 3,000 km floor is OSW gate geometry

claims.scope: A derived minimum north–south span for the coherent shelf-break jet only; not a measured streamline or a published whole-current length. Separation and extension shift over time.
claims.source_locator: Section 1 Introduction, opening EAC paragraph (15–32°S); 1,800 km floor is OSW meridional gate geometry

claims.scope: Approximate 6,000 km Humboldt Current belt from southern Chile toward northern Peru and the Galápagos, reported in an embedded Purca et al. manuscript in Purca Cuicapusa's 2005 thesis. This is a broad eastern South Pacific current-system extent, not a measured core streamline or the Peru Coastal Current alone; the manuscript separately describes its 1,000 km Peru study area.
claims.source_locator: PDF page 65, embedded Purca et al. manuscript, Introduction opening paragraph (ca. 6,000 km belt); PDF page 66 distinguishes its 1,000 km Peru study area

claims.scope: A 1989 paper hypothesizes a 5,000 km buoyancy-driven coastal connection from southern Greenland to the Middle Atlantic Bight based on limited oxygen-isotope evidence. This proposed system length is unranked and is not the length of the Labrador Current alone.
claims.source_locator: Abstract, proposed 5,000 km buoyancy-driven coastal current from southern Greenland to the Middle Atlantic Bight

claims.scope: Tomczak and Godfrey report approximately 1,200 km from the Florida Straits along the coast to separation near Cape Hatteras. This is the Florida Current segment of the Gulf Stream System, not a whole-system length or a measured reference streamline. NOAA's glossary independently names the same segment; NASA and NOAA Coast Pilot sometimes use Gulf Stream more broadly for the Florida Straits flow.
claims.source_locator: Chapter 14, The Atlantic Ocean, PDF page 11 (printed page 239), paragraph beginning Recirculation of Gulf Stream water (1,200 km downstream to Cape Hatteras)

claims.scope: The study distinguishes the outer East Greenland Current from the coastal branch and assesses the system between the 78.5°N Fram Strait section and Cape Farewell. The coast-following route may be longer than the north–south separation; no comparable whole-current centerline length is admitted, so this regional floor is unranked.
claims.source_locator: Section 2, paragraph defining East Greenland shelf from Fram Strait 78.5°N to Cape Farewell 59°N; 2,100 km floor is OSW meridional gate geometry
PDF page 36, Conclusions opening paragraph (current along entire 1,000 km southeast Greenland shelf)

claims.scope: Published lower bound for southward flow along Western Australia's continental shelf, from tropical to cool-temperate coasts; distinct from the northward West Australian Current offshore. A lower bound is not a ranked whole-current estimate.
claims.source_locator: PDF page 108 (viewer page including cover); source states more than 2,000 km

claims.scope: Continuous austral-winter shelf-edge flow from North West Cape to southern Tasmania, comprising the Leeuwin, South Australian, and Zeehan currents; not the length of Leeuwin alone.
claims.source_locator: Abstract [1] and Section 9 Discussion and Conclusion [53] (5,500 km winter boundary-flow system)

claims.scope: Approximate basin-wide eastward pathway from north of Papua New Guinea to the South American coast described in Grenier et al. (2011). The source's 14,000 km is a broad path estimate, not a traced instantaneous core or the length of the Atlantic or Indian Equatorial Undercurrent. A 0°N, 140°W mooring locates the current independently.

A later wave–current dynamics paper describes the Pacific EUC as traversing the equatorial Pacific over about 13,000 km. It does not define the same exact core or gates as Grenier et al.; retained as a source-specific whole-basin approximation rather than an independent rank.
claims.source_locator: Introduction, opening Equatorial Undercurrent description, entire Pacific equatorial length about 13,000 km

claims.scope: The study identifies the Benguela Current system at 30°, 24°, and 19°S across decadal inverse solutions, with no continuity north of 19°S. claims.source_locator: Section 3.1.3 and Figure 5, Benguela Current system at 30°S, 24°S, and 19°S; OSW WGS84 meridional gate calculation

claims.scope: The study identifies southward Brazil Current transport at 19°, 24°, and 30°S. Confluence location and downstream identity vary. Section observations are from different cruises and do not establish a simultaneous centerline; the derived floor is unranked.
claims.source_locator: Section 3.1.2 and Figure 5, Brazil Current at 19°S, 24°S, and 30°S; OSW WGS84 meridional gate calculation

claims.scope: The study identifies southward deep western boundary flow at 47°, 36°, and 24.5°N in decadal inverse solutions. This is a North Atlantic segment only; sections from different cruises do not establish one simultaneous continuous path or a whole-Atlantic current length. The derived floor is unranked.
claims.source_locator: Section 3.2.3 and Figure 8, DWBC at 47°N, 36°N, and 24.5°N; OSW WGS84 meridional gate calculation

claims.scope: Stabeno et al. (2016) report an approximate 1,700 km coastal system between Seward and Samalga Pass. This is the northern Gulf of Alaska/eastern Aleutian scope, separate from the offshore Alaska Current and Alaskan Stream. It does not cover every coastal flow sharing the Alaska Coastal Current name, including Arctic usage. The paper integrates intermittent observations from 1984-2014; this extent is not a measured simultaneous reference streamline or dated footprint.
claims.source_locator: Accepted manuscript, PDF page 2, Abstract, lines 25-28 (~1700 km, Seward to Samalga Pass); PDF page 3, Introduction, lines 51-59 defines the regional continuity scope.

measurements.scope: Approximate circumpolar path; source calls it the longest wind-driven current.
measurements.source_locator: Section 1 Introduction, opening sentence (approximately 25,000 km)

measurements.scope: NASA/JPL's 2019 overview says the Antarctic Circumpolar Current spans about 13,000 miles (21,000 km). It does not specify a reference streamline or contour, so this alternate whole-current approximation is retained separately from the ranked 25,000 km research estimate.
measurements.source_locator: NASA/JPL article, paragraph beginning The Antarctic Circumpolar Current flows in a loop (13,000 miles / 21,000 km)

measurements.scope: Approximate California Current System extent from Baja California Sur to northern Vancouver Island; not a measured California Current core axis.
measurements.source_locator: PDF page 3, background box under California Current (California Current System extends 3,000 km)

measurements.scope: Tomczak and Godfrey report approximately 2,500 km for the Gulf Stream proper as an open-ocean free jet downstream of Cape Hatteras toward the Newfoundland Rise/Grand Banks near 50°W. This excludes the Florida Current and North Atlantic Current; it is a textbook path-scale description, not a measured reference streamline. NOAA's glossary uses the same strict segment definition, while NASA and NOAA Coast Pilot sometimes use Gulf Stream more broadly.
measurements.source_locator: Chapter 14, The Atlantic Ocean, PDF page 11 (printed page 239), paragraph beginning Recirculation of Gulf Stream water (next 2,500 km Gulf Stream proper)

measurements.scope: sampled_reach
measurements.source_locator: PDF page 3, Section 2.1 Underwater Glider Data and Methods, paragraph on 52 missions sampling a roughly 2,000 km Gulf Stream reach

measurements.scope: Approximate Kuroshio journey from about 12°N to 35°N in the western North Pacific; not a measured whole-current axis, and the Kuroshio Extension is separate.
measurements.source_locator: PDF page 3, Introduction opening paragraph (3,000 km journey from about 12°N to 35°N)

measurements.scope: The research description spans roughly 27°S–40°S; the coastal path is longer than its north–south separation. Retroflection, leakage, and the eastward Agulhas Return Current are distinct from this boundary-current core. The derived floor is unranked. A 2021 review also describes a roughly 1,000 km coastal segment. That narrower usage conflicts with the broader 27°S–40°S derived floor, so the two numbers are displayed as source-specific scopes and neither is ranked as a common whole-current length.
measurements.source_locator: Section The Agulhas Current, opening paragraph (27–40°S); 1,400 km floor is OSW meridional gate geometry

measurements.scope: Coastal western boundary current along southeastern Africa; narrower than the 27°S–40°S span used for the existing broad lower bound. End gates and centerline are not specified.
measurements.source_locator: Section 2.1.1 Background, opening paragraph (1,000 km western boundary current)

measurements.scope: The hydrographic survey distinguishes the Agulhas Return Current from the Agulhas Current and traces its weakening eastward flow toward the Crozet Basin. This derived distance floor is not a measured streamline, whole-current length, or the length of the westward Agulhas Current.
measurements.source_locator: PDF pages 20–22, Figure 14 and Section 6 Conclusions, Agulhas Return Current surveyed eastward from 18°E to 76°E; 3,000 km floor is OSW gate geometry

measurements.scope: A derived minimum north–south span for the coherent shelf-break jet only; not a measured streamline or a published whole-current length. Separation and extension shift over time.
measurements.source_locator: Section 1 Introduction, opening EAC paragraph (15–32°S); 1,800 km floor is OSW meridional gate geometry

measurements.scope: Approximate 6,000 km Humboldt Current belt from southern Chile toward northern Peru and the Galápagos, reported in an embedded Purca et al. manuscript in Purca Cuicapusa's 2005 thesis. This is a broad eastern South Pacific current-system extent, not a measured core streamline or the Peru Coastal Current alone; the manuscript separately describes its 1,000 km Peru study area.
measurements.source_locator: PDF page 65, embedded Purca et al. manuscript, Introduction opening paragraph (ca. 6,000 km belt); PDF page 66 distinguishes its 1,000 km Peru study area

measurements.scope: A 1989 paper hypothesizes a 5,000 km buoyancy-driven coastal connection from southern Greenland to the Middle Atlantic Bight based on limited oxygen-isotope evidence. This proposed system length is unranked and is not the length of the Labrador Current alone.
measurements.source_locator: Abstract, proposed 5,000 km buoyancy-driven coastal current from southern Greenland to the Middle Atlantic Bight

measurements.source_locator: Abstract [1] and Section 4 Discussion and Conclusions [15], October 2009 section at 24.5°W; each current has 110 km meridional width

measurements.scope: Tomczak and Godfrey report approximately 1,200 km from the Florida Straits along the coast to separation near Cape Hatteras. This is the Florida Current segment of the Gulf Stream System, not a whole-system length or a measured reference streamline. NOAA's glossary independently names the same segment; NASA and NOAA Coast Pilot sometimes use Gulf Stream more broadly for the Florida Straits flow.
measurements.source_locator: Chapter 14, The Atlantic Ocean, PDF page 11 (printed page 239), paragraph beginning Recirculation of Gulf Stream water (1,200 km downstream to Cape Hatteras)

measurements.scope: The study distinguishes the outer East Greenland Current from the coastal branch and assesses the system between the 78.5°N Fram Strait section and Cape Farewell. The coast-following route may be longer than the north–south separation; no comparable whole-current centerline length is admitted, so this regional floor is unranked.
measurements.source_locator: Section 2, paragraph defining East Greenland shelf from Fram Strait 78.5°N to Cape Farewell 59°N; 2,100 km floor is OSW meridional gate geometry

measurements.scope: sampled_reach
measurements.source_locator: PDF page 36, Conclusions opening paragraph (current along entire 1,000 km southeast Greenland shelf)

measurements.scope: Published lower bound for southward flow along Western Australia's continental shelf, from tropical to cool-temperate coasts; distinct from the northward West Australian Current offshore. A lower bound is not a ranked whole-current estimate.
measurements.source_locator: PDF page 108 (viewer page including cover); source states more than 2,000 km

measurements.scope: Continuous austral-winter shelf-edge flow from North West Cape to southern Tasmania, comprising the Leeuwin, South Australian, and Zeehan currents; not the length of Leeuwin alone.
measurements.source_locator: Abstract [1] and Section 9 Discussion and Conclusion [53] (5,500 km winter boundary-flow system)

measurements.scope: Approximate basin-wide eastward pathway from north of Papua New Guinea to the South American coast described in Grenier et al. (2011). The source's 14,000 km is a broad path estimate, not a traced instantaneous core or the length of the Atlantic or Indian Equatorial Undercurrent. A 0°N, 140°W mooring locates the current independently.
measurements.source_locator: Section 1 Introduction, paragraph [2] (14,000 km pathway)

measurements.scope: A later wave–current dynamics paper describes the Pacific EUC as traversing the equatorial Pacific over about 13,000 km. It does not define the same exact core or gates as Grenier et al.; retained as a source-specific whole-basin approximation rather than an independent rank.
measurements.source_locator: Introduction, opening Equatorial Undercurrent description, entire Pacific equatorial length about 13,000 km

measurements.scope: The study identifies the Benguela Current system at 30°, 24°, and 19°S across decadal inverse solutions, with no continuity north of 19°S. The current and Benguela ecosystem have different extents. Section observations are from different cruises and do not establish a simultaneous centerline; the derived floor is unranked.
measurements.source_locator: Section 3.1.3 and Figure 5, Benguela Current system at 30°S, 24°S, and 19°S; OSW WGS84 meridional gate calculation

measurements.scope: The study identifies southward Brazil Current transport at 19°, 24°, and 30°S. Confluence location and downstream identity vary. Section observations are from different cruises and do not establish a simultaneous centerline; the derived floor is unranked.
measurements.source_locator: Section 3.1.2 and Figure 5, Brazil Current at 19°S, 24°S, and 30°S; OSW WGS84 meridional gate calculation

measurements.scope: The study identifies southward deep western boundary flow at 47°, 36°, and 24.5°N in decadal inverse solutions. This is a North Atlantic segment only; sections from different cruises do not establish one simultaneous continuous path or a whole-Atlantic current length. The derived floor is unranked.
measurements.source_locator: Section 3.2.3 and Figure 8, DWBC at 47°N, 36°N, and 24.5°N; OSW WGS84 meridional gate calculation

measurements.scope: Stabeno et al. (2016) report an approximate 1,700 km coastal system between Seward and Samalga Pass. This is the northern Gulf of Alaska/eastern Aleutian scope, separate from the offshore Alaska Current and Alaskan Stream. It does not cover every coastal flow sharing the Alaska Coastal Current name, including Arctic usage. The paper integrates intermittent observations from 1984-2014; this extent is not a measured simultaneous reference streamline or dated footprint.
measurements.source_locator: Accepted manuscript, PDF page 2, Abstract, lines 25-28 (~1700 km, Seward to Samalga Pass); PDF page 3, Introduction, lines 51-59 defines the regional continuity scope.

measurements.method: Source review's approximate system-span statement, retained with its Antarctic Peninsula continuity limit; no route digitization or instantaneous path measurement
measurements.scope: Review-reported upper-continental-slope system span; not a measured reference streamline or dated footprint. The Antarctic Peninsula interrupts circumpolar continuity.
measurements.source_locator: Section 1.1 ASC Characteristics, first sentence; Figure 2 caption and following paragraph qualify continuity

measurements.scope: Source-reported approximate 2,000 km northward loop of the northern Antarctic Circumpolar Current branch in the Argentine Basin, from a 2009 EGU conference abstract. named_eddy_footprint_candidates.coordinate_reference_status: Longitude/latitude inferred from figure axes; source figure does not specify a geodetic datum. Decimal output precision does not imply survey accuracy.
named_eddy_footprint_candidates.method: Segment the single closed blue loop by three RGB thresholds; trace its outside pixel contour; linearly georeference from the manually read panel ticks; intersect the enclosed polygon with the coast-masked approximate OSW state shapes under 16 independent ±3-pixel axis-tick perturbations per threshold.
named_eddy_footprint_candidates.physical_limit: Dated 2-D instantaneous SSH contour proxy only. Axis-tick sensitivity can place part of this near-boundary contour in CARB, so whole-footprint CAMR containment is unresolved. This is not the material coherent-core curve, a 3-D ring volume, or a claim for August/October. Source JPEG quality, manual axis reading, line thickness, and schematic OSW state geometry limit precision.
named_eddy_footprint_candidates.source_locator: Figure 2, 29 May 2013 panel, outermost closed blue instantaneous SSH contour

named_eddy_footprint_candidates.coordinate_reference_status: Longitude/latitude inferred by linear calibration of source figure axes. Source datum/projection are unspecified; seven-decimal output is display precision only.
named_eddy_footprint_candidates.method: Threshold maximum RGB channel below 40/70/100 within the pinned interior ROI; require one dominant closed hollow loop; trace outer and inner stroke edges using CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE (exact collinear source-pixel compression), without morphological repair; preserve rejected non-simple threshold-100 rings; transfer common figure tick calibration; test nominal plus sixteen independent +/-3-pixel anchor shifts per accepted edge/threshold; intersect approximate coast-masked OSW display polygons.
named_eddy_footprint_candidates.physical_limit: Dated instantaneous figure-derived SSH contour proxy during the Ursa shedding event. Attribution to the detached named ring is an editorial interpretation requiring scientific review. Source prints 0.65 cm with unresolved unit; no numerical SSH contour was reconstructed. Not a verified whole-ring physical footprint, material coherent core, 3-D volume, lifetime extent or NASA individual identity. Tested scenarios omit source field error, unknown datum/projection, instrument-dot artifacts and OSW boundary uncertainty; no statistical confidence or physical uncertainty bound follows.

named_eddy_source_observations.interpretation: The authors identify the Loop Current ring as Kraken and analyze a resilient material core during this interval. OSW georeferences selected red Figure 2 curve pixels as a state-location candidate; the authors' closed boundary coordinates are not reconstructed.
named_eddy_source_observations.reported_measure: Approximately 100 km mean radius of the coherent core, a definition distinct from the outer instantaneous SSH footprint.

named_eddy_source_observations.interpretation: The authors map the Thor shedding event in January–June 2020 and describe detachment, reattachment, final separation, and westward propagation. The date bounds describe the paper's figure window, not a measured lifetime.
Satellite SST and concurrent drifter velocities support Thor being separated by this date; this does not establish that every later detachment was final.
Thor had deformed and nearly split into two eddies by this date; near-splitting is not a verified division into two independently named rings.

The authors map the Ursa shedding event in January–May 2021, including temporary detachment and reattachment. The date bounds describe the paper's figure window, not a measured lifetime or independent final separation date.
The later paper identifies a brief first separation followed by reattachment.
The later paper reports final Ursa separation on this date; the date is source-reported, not a geometric reconstruction by OSW.

The authors locate Cameron's center approximately at mooring A on January 20 and describe its later west-southwest translation and deformation through March 1. These are western Gulf observations, not initial separation or whole-lifetime dates.

named_current_source_observations.source_locator: Abstract; section 2 Data and method; section 3.1 Mean structure; Figures 1-3
named_current_source_observations.spatial_basis: OSW projects the three paper-reported instrument positions into the approximate coast-masked state polygons. All three positions fall in CHIN. These are mooring locations, not the Kuroshio axis or an interpolated cross-stream boundary.
named_current_source_observations.state_boundary_limit: The CHIN link is a lookup of three instrument points against approximate display geography; it is not whole-current containment, intersection, or a measured state boundary. The paper places the current core west of the array.
named_current_source_observations.time_detail: The paper reports January 2018 to May 2020, without exact deployment and recovery days here. This is the reported study window, not a claim of continuous valid coverage at every depth or station.

widths.name: North Cape Current — Northern branch
widths.range_interpretation: Approximate fitted effective scale; no fit confidence interval or annual variability range supplied.
widths.geographic_scope: Northern branch near the western Hopen Deep / Spitsbergen Bank polar frontal zone, Barents Sea. Not the Central branch or whole North Cape system.
widths.section_orientation: Distance from frontal-section center across individual crossings; northward geographic velocity component fitted. Exact paired geographic boundaries unresolved.
widths.layer: Composite vertical support unresolved. Fig. 9 specifies a 20–80 m average for LS05; Fig. 10 does not explicitly establish that same fixed layer for all 15 crossings. Instrument generally sampled from about 20 m to 150 m or 15 m above bottom.
widths.time_convention: 15 frontal crossings during summer expeditions in 2007. Paper describes a 29 May–10 June 2007 cruise, but exact composite sampling bounds are unresolved; not a recurring seasonal width.
widths.boundary_rule: Source approximates the mean northward velocity profile by V(x)=17 exp(-(x/8)^2), x in km and V in cm/s, and calls 8 km mean effective width. OSW infers center-to-e-folding scale from the equation; no paired-edge full span is admitted.
widths.source_citation: Morozov, Pavlov, Pavlova and Fedorov (2017), Polar Frontal Zone of the Barents Sea Western Trough Based on the Direct Measurements in 2007, Physical Oceanography 2, 36–50, doi:10.22449/1573-160X-2017-2-36-50.
widths.source_locator: Abstract; Introduction pp. 36–37; Instruments p. 37; Stationary currents p. 38; Currents pp. 45–47, Fig. 9 and Fig. 10, especially Gaussian-fit paragraph on p. 47.
widths.extraction_method: Transcribed source fit scale and 15-crossing count; metric interpretation inferred algebraically from stated Gaussian equation. No figure digitized or converted full width added.
remaining_gates: Resolve exact composite depth averaging and crossing dates from underlying data.
Define comparable paired boundaries before any full-width comparison.
Review branch identity and along-route support; canonical admission remains pending.

widths.name: Deep Western Boundary Current
widths.range_interpretation: Approximate width of the historical upper-core float composite. Repeated 100 km subset entries do not establish constant width, annual extrema or numerical width uncertainty.
widths.geographic_scope: Tropical western Atlantic upper-core DWBC; Table 2 selection domain 2 S-12 N west of 43 W; section 3.2 labels a 0-7 N / 12-month composite. Source domains retained without forced equivalence.
widths.section_orientation: Distance seaward of 1800 m isobath; velocity rotated parallel and normal to that contour.
widths.layer: Nominal 1800 m SOFAR floats; failed active depth control and source-estimated sinking about 230 m over 21 months. No fixed numerical width layer.
widths.time_convention: Table 2 historical composite label January 1989-October 1990, overlapping three unequal subsets. No exact width observation dates or recurring seasonal calendar extracted.
widths.boundary_rule: Width between zero-velocity points in the composite along-boundary velocity profile, flanked by weak counterflow/recirculation; 10 km averaging bins do not supply a width error.
widths.source_citation: Richardson, P. L. and Schmitz, W. J., Jr. (1993), Deep Cross-Equatorial Flow in the Atlantic Measured With SOFAR Floats, Journal of Geophysical Research 98(C5), 8371-8387, doi:10.1029/93JC00051.
widths.source_locator: Final original PDF p5 / printed p8375, section 3.2 continuation; Table 2 PDF p8 / p8378; nominal depth and processing p2; subset sampling p6 and Figure 6 p7.
widths.extraction_method: Visually reviewed numerical passage, Table 2 and methods transcribed; no plot-edge digitization or raw velocity recalculation.
widths.source_quality_note: Composite and subset sampling are sparse and nonuniform. Nominal float depths drifted. Source-label and count inconsistencies are preserved; velocity/transport standard errors are not width errors.
remaining_gates: Acquire and reprocess raw calibrated float records with their changing depths.
Recover geographically supported zero-velocity edges before footprints or physical state intersections.
Repeated compatible sections and width errors before annual margins or seasonal playback.

widths.source_quality_note: Approximate meridional breadth of a long-term geostrophic mean; no numeric width uncertainty, fixed section or monthly widths. Spatially varying density-surface depth is distinct from a fixed depth.

reference_routes.scope: NOAA glossary regional extent from about 160 degrees E to an OSW gate at 145 degrees W, somewhat beyond the source's approximate 150 degrees W region. Whole-current axis, endpoints, width and annual ranges remain unresolved.

seasonal_routes.time_convention: Northeast winter monsoon convention; not a simultaneous dated observation or an annual-average route.
seasonal_routes.layer: Surface/upper-layer seasonal coastal reference geography; the source describes a shallow winter equatorial current, but no fixed-depth velocity axis is reconstructed.
seasonal_routes.source_locator: Section 4.2.1, printed pages 48-49 (PDF indices 47-48): southward surface flow reaches EACC confluence at 2-4 S; winter coastal divergence near 6-8 N. Section 4.2.2 distinguishes modeled coastal continuation and northern countercurrent.
seasonal_routes.label: Somali Current — Northeast winter monsoon

comparability.reason: Winter coastal branch and June-July southern limb have different source-defined spatial scopes; their nominal lengths or scenario bounds do not define annual whole-current extrema.

seasonal_routes.time_convention: June-July monsoon-onset two-gyre convention. Does not assume rare late-summer gyre coalescence or persistent whole-coast continuity.
seasonal_routes.layer: Upper-layer southern seasonal coastal geography; no fixed-depth or velocity-derived axis.
seasonal_routes.source_locator: Section 4.1.1, printed page 38 (PDF index 37): June-July cross-equatorial limb departs the coast south of 4 N, partitions into offshore outflow/recirculation and has little exchange with Great Whirl. Printed pages 41-43 discuss non-universal gyre coalescence.
seasonal_routes.label: Somali Current — June-July southern limb

comparability.reason: Winter coastal branch and June-July southern limb have different source-defined spatial scopes; their nominal lengths or scenario bounds do not define annual whole-current extrema.

seasonal_routes.width_scope_note: Approximate 64 km is historical California-Oregon regional context; it is not applied uniformly to the editorial route or used as an occupied footprint.
seasonal_routes.time_convention: October-March California-Oregon regional seasonal description in the February 1978 report; strongest flow described in January. Historical summary, not a dated trajectory, current-year observation or modern monthly climatology.
seasonal_routes.layer: Seasonal northward surface-current regional context; not the separately described California Undercurrent below 200 m or a reconstructed velocity axis.
seasonal_routes.source_locator: Appendix II section II.1, printed II-1 to II-2 / PDF pages 12-13: northward seasonal surface strip along California and Oregon from October to March; Vancouver Island penetration is conditional.
seasonal_routes.label: Davidson Current — October-March (1978 regional summary)

comparability.reason: Only historical October-March California-Oregon reference geography and width context are available. April-September width and seasonal route geometry remain unknown; no modern annual cycle, seasonal extrema or uniform width footprint established.

seasonal_routes.phase_label: Southwest Monsoon Current · June–September eastward regional reach
seasonal_routes.time_convention: Boreal summer source convention, June–September. Historical review and section context, not a simultaneous dated trajectory or current-year climatology.
seasonal_routes.layer: Seasonal near-surface regional geography. Historical section evidence is shallow and depth dependent; no fixed-depth velocity axis reconstructed and undercurrents excluded.
seasonal_routes.source_locator: Schott and McCreary (2001), section 5.1.5, printed pp. 63–65 / PDF indices 62–64: seasonal directions/months, Sri Lanka bottleneck and separate upper-layer/undercurrent flows. August 1993 and January 1991 sections provide local latitude context, not regional axis vertices.
seasonal_routes.label: Monsoon Current — Southwest Monsoon Current · June–September eastward regional reach

comparability.reason: Two source-defined seasonal phases with editorial 77–83 E regional drawings. Their different latitude choices and scenario envelopes are not observed annual length minima/maxima. March–May and October geometry and all seasonal widths remain unresolved; month labels do not provide monthly velocity fields.

seasonal_routes.phase_label: Northeast Monsoon Current · November–February westward regional reach
seasonal_routes.time_convention: Boreal winter source convention, November–February. Historical review and section context, not a simultaneous dated trajectory or current-year climatology.
seasonal_routes.layer: Seasonal near-surface regional geography. Historical section evidence is shallow and depth dependent; no fixed-depth velocity axis reconstructed and undercurrents excluded.
seasonal_routes.source_locator: Schott and McCreary (2001), section 5.1.5, printed pp. 63–65 / PDF indices 62–64: seasonal directions/months, Sri Lanka bottleneck and separate upper-layer/undercurrent flows. August 1993 and January 1991 sections provide local latitude context, not regional axis vertices.
seasonal_routes.label: Monsoon Current — Northeast Monsoon Current · November–February westward regional reach

comparability.reason: Two source-defined seasonal phases with editorial 77–83 E regional drawings. Their different latitude choices and scenario envelopes are not observed annual length minima/maxima. March–May and October geometry and all seasonal widths remain unresolved; month labels do not provide monthly velocity fields.

seasonal_routes.time_convention: Source boreal winter December-March convention; Gauss-Markov seasonal climatology using 1993-2018 drifter context. Not a dated trajectory or complete annual route series.
seasonal_routes.layer: Surface drifter climatology with GDP drogue support near 15 m and wind-slip-corrected undrogued observations; not a uniform fixed-depth current axis or full vertical extent. OSCAR upper-layer and deeper current diagnostics remain separate.
seasonal_routes.source_locator: Sections 2.1-2.2: drifter support, 1993-2018 selection, fitted seasonal fields and December-March winter. Section 3 seasonal discussion after Figures 5-6: eastward SECC reaches about 90 E before recirculating into SEC; Figure 13 caption.
seasonal_routes.label: Indian Ocean South Equatorial Countercurrent — December-March eastward surface reach

comparability.reason: One December-March surface studied reach with editorial gates and vertices. Other seasonal axes and paired-edge widths are unavailable. Its 4400-4500 km drawing envelope is not annual length variation.

geometry_frames.label: Gulf Stream System — 2025-01-15 frozen-field diagnostic
geometry_frames.layer: Altimetry-derived absolute surface geostrophic velocity, NOAA LSA experimental RADS 4.7.0, RADS 4.7.1, 0.25-degree grid.
geometry_frames.method: Frozen-time WGS84 midpoint integration, 10 km steps, fixed seed [-72.875,36.875], 0.15 m/s stop threshold, first -50-degree longitude crossing, speed/missing-data stop or hard 4000 km distance cap.
geometry_frames.sampling_note: Fifteenth day of each month in 2025, selected before acquisition. Twelve daily snapshots, not monthly means, climatology or annual extrema.
geometry_frames.limitations: Twelve selected daily fields do not establish monthly means, seasonal climatology, annual extrema, whole-current axis or width. Finite seed/step sensitivity is reported; positional uncertainty is not quantified.
geometry_frames.attribution: Altimetry data are provided by the NOAA Laboratory for Satellite Altimetry. Acknowledge NOAA CoastWatch.

diagnostic_sensitivity.rounding_rule: Outward to 10 km; only gate-reaching traces enter the span; all failures retained.

document.source_citation: Deng, Hwang, Coleman and Featherstone (2008), Seasonal and Interannual Variations of the Leeuwin Current off Western Australia from TOPEX/Poseidon Satellite Altimetry, TAO 19, 135-149, doi:10.3319/TAO.2008.19.1-2.135(SA).
document.source_locator: Figure 7d, printed page 144; April/September prose on page 143; method equations 1-3 on page 138.
document.averaging_order: fit per altimeter cycle, derive width, then average widths by calendar month across years
document.scope_note: Historical calendar-month means of fitted widths at one crossing. Reading intervals are graph extraction margins. July and September intervals overlap; graph readings do not establish a uniquely narrowest month. No whole-current annual extrema or current footprint inferred.

document.source_citation: Liu and Gan (2012), Variability of the Kuroshio in the East China Sea derived from satellite altimetry data, Deep-Sea Research I 59, 25-36, doi:10.1016/j.dsr.2011.10.008.
document.source_locator: Figure 6a, printed page 30; method section 2.2, page 26; seasonal prose section 3.2, page 29.
document.averaging_order: Stream-coordinate diagnostics including section width calculated every 7 days, then temporal and along-stream summaries; not width diagnosed from a seasonal mean velocity field.
document.source_quality_note: Weekly averaged and smoothed surface geostrophic product; ageostrophic flow is not included in the width diagnosis. Interpolation to 0.1 degree does not add independent observation resolution. Exact spatial/temporal weighting and season-to-month convention remain unresolved.
document.scope_note: Sparse readings along regional seasonal profiles. Missing pixels stay missing; these samples do not supply geographic edges, spring/autumn regional means, full-current dimensions or annual physical extrema.

document.layer: Satellite-derived near-surface product with nominal 15 m coordinate; not a direct 15 m instrument section or depth-resolved current.
remaining_gates: Independent boundary, branch and product-error review.
Repeat years/sections and compatible products before representative seasonal ranges.
No route or canonical measurement admission from this section alone.

document.threshold_rule: 0.5 times maximum positive northward sample among provider-usable casts, separately by occupation; walk eastward to first bracket without crossing missing/caution casts
remaining_gates: Independent review of section membership, tide/error-velocity impact, threshold and sampled-peak representativeness.
Diagnose both depth-compatible boundaries and sampling sufficiency before full-width measurement.
Recover along-current axes and repeated annual support; two May occupations are not a seasonal cycle.

note.label: Offshore West Australian versus coastal Leeuwin flow
note.summary: Modern West Australian Current means broad northward offshore flow, distinct from coastal southward Leeuwin. Andrews (1977) used the name for a cyclonic stream turning poleward: its reported 800 km trough extent and 100-200 km stream width remain historical source context, not admitted dimensions for this current or seasonal extrema. Whole-current axis, endpoints, width and annual ranges remain unresolved.

document.name: West Australian Current

primary_definition.interpretation: Broad offshore northward subtropical-gyre flow; distinct from coastal southward Leeuwin. Definition supplies no diagnosed axis, numeric endpoint coordinates or physical width.

coastal_study.interpretation: Coastal shelf-edge system and its regional names; its 5500 km winter system length is not transferable to offshore West Australian Current.

seasonal_context_lead.citation: D’Adamo and Onton (2003), MMS-75/2003, dated 15 July 2003
seasonal_context_lead.locator: Section 4 and Figure 12 caption, printed pp. 5 and 21 / PDF pp. 8 and 24
provenance_chain: US Navy (1976) Climatic Atlas of the World
seasonal_context_lead.interpretation: Seasonal branching descriptions are inherited context, not newly acquired velocity geometry. Figure legend includes probable directions/speeds with insufficient data. Original atlas methodology and applicable samples require review.

historical_naming_lead.access: publisher_indexed_abstract_read_2026-10-03; direct publisher full page unavailable; full paper not inspected
historical_naming_lead.interpretation: Abstract describes a cyclonic stream extending northeast from the Naturaliste Plateau and turning poleward at the coast. Its use of West Australian Current differs from the modern offshore northward definition; equivalence remains unreviewed.
historical_naming_lead.citation: Andrews (1977), Eddy structure and the West Australian current, Deep Sea Research 24(12), 1133-1148, doi:10.1016/0146-6291(77)90517-3.

reported_context.sampling: Four cruises in the summers of 1972 and 1973; individual cruise dates unavailable in inspected abstract.

rejected_inferences: No reuse of Leeuwin or 5500 km coastal-system path length.
No conversion of broad eastern Indian Ocean description into physical width or a representative single core.
No use of seasonal 20 S branching context as a universal whole-current endpoint.
No figure tracing or seasonal interpolation from inherited atlas patterns.
No transfer of the 1977 reported 800 km trough extent or 100-200 km cyclonic stream width into modern offshore-current dimensions before identity equivalence and full source methodology are reviewed.
The historical width interval is not a seasonal minimum/maximum range; a 370 m scale depth is not a uniform axis layer.
No substitution of coastal summer Capes/Ningaloo flow or deeper Leeuwin Undercurrent for the modern offshore West Australian Current.
Model particle release boundaries, sector limits and transport agreement are not current endpoint, width-edge or centerline diagnoses.
remaining_gates: Retrieve the full 1977 paper and resolve its poleward cyclonic-stream naming against the modern offshore northward flow; keep its reported dimensions in unadmitted source context meanwhile.
Choose representative layer and time support for a broad flow; consider a diagnostic flow corridor before a centerline.
Retrieve appropriate offshore velocity data and justify northern/southern interface gates independently of coastal-current geometry.
Read original seasonal atlas/data methodology before generating dated or seasonal routes.
Keep physical width, annual extrema and canonical measurement admission unresolved.

modern_pathway_context.citation: Yit Sen Bull and van Sebille (2016), Sources, fate, and pathways of Leeuwin Current water in the Indian Ocean and Great Australian Bight: A Lagrangian study in an eddy-resolving ocean model, doi:10.1002/2015JC011486.
modern_pathway_context.access: Full publisher page retrieved; Introduction and sections 2.1-2.4 read on 2026-10-03; no figures digitized or model data acquired.
modern_pathway_context.locator: Introduction; 2.2 Eulerian TROPAC01 Validation at 32 S; 2.3 Lagrangian Particle Model; 2.4 coastal sectors.
modern_pathway_context.interpretation: Leeuwin, its deeper equatorward undercurrent, and inshore summer Capes/Ningaloo flows are separately named. Subtropical onshore supply and particle connectivity do not diagnose a whole West Australian Current axis.
modern_pathway_context.validation_caution: Section 2.2 reports lower modeled flow speeds compensated by broader flow in transport validation. Agreement of integrated transport does not independently validate width or a centerline.
modern_pathway_context.model_support: TROPAC01 1/10-degree model; 1960-2009 hindcast at five-day temporal means. This is model support, not West Australian Current observation dates.

section.orientation: fixed meridional section, not a fitted flow-normal section
section.location_role: Ingoy region coastal-to-offshore diagnostic; selected limits are not current boundaries

model_frames.sampling_rule: Fifteenth day at 12:00 UTC, 10 m depth, four-cell stride; fixed before acquisition. Twelve hourly model snapshots, not monthly means or climatology.
model_frames.interpolation: Bilinear in projected grid coordinates, four wet non-fill corners required; 3.2 km decimated source spacing, approximately 1.1 km display spacing adds no resolution.
model_frames.limitations: Hourly hindcast snapshots include tides and weather-driven variability. They are not monthly means, observations, a climatology or a current footprint. Low salinity and flow components alone do not identify current boundaries. Width, whole-current length and annual extrema remain unknown. Missing four-corner support remains a gap.
